excerpt: Quell was a London fitness-gaming startup whose wearable resistance-band controller turned workouts into the fantasy fighting game Shardfall. Funding, product and current status.
content:
Quell was a London company that tried to turn home exercise into a video game. Players strapped on a harness with resistance bands attached to hand-held controllers, then punched, blocked and dodged to fight their way through a fantasy game called Shardfall on a PC, Mac or mobile screen. TechCrunch reported in 2020 that built-in sensors measured punch speed and accuracy and that the bands could be swapped to make the workout harder. The device was later marketed as Quell Impact.

The company was co-founded by Cameron Brookhouse, its CEO, and Doug Stidolph. Its 2020 Kickstarter raised £501,341, about $670,000, from nearly 3,000 backers. In December 2020 it raised a $3 million seed round from investors including Tencent, Khosla Ventures, Heartcore, Twitch co-founders Kevin Lin and Emmett Shear, and Naval Ravikant, TechCrunch reported, and said it planned to ship its first hardware by the end of 2021. In February 2023 it raised a $10 million Series A led by Tencent, bringing total funding to $15.6 million, according to Tech.eu, which also reported 10,000 pre-orders. TechCrunch put the pre-order price at $249, with shipping planned for 2023.

Current status: when we checked in October 2026, the original quell.tech address no longer resolved, and the later product site, playquell.com, redirected to an unrelated betting website, which suggests the domain has lapsed. We found no official announcement about the company's status, so treat Quell's products and services as unavailable unless the company says otherwise. Backers and owners should check the Kickstarter page's updates for official news.

This page is research, not a review. We have not used Quell; facts come from the reporting listed under Sources and the company's archived website.
